message.reasoning:
I am evaluating a Monopoly trade offer from p2.

The offer is $40 and MARVIN_GARDENS for PARK_PLACE. I am weighing this against my current holdings.

I have the full orange set but New York Avenue is mortgaged. I am missing Virginia from the pink set. I have $551 in cash. p2 has Boardwalk and $236. p3 has Med/Baltic hotels and $813. p4 owns a light blue monopoly and $1435.

This trade is risky. Park Place would complete a dark blue monopoly for p2, which they could unmortgage and build on immediately. Marvin Gardens is a yellow property, but I lack other yellows to form that set.

The $40 offer is negligible. Strategy notes explicitly forbid selling Park Place to p2 because they own Boardwalk. Unmortgaging Park Place would cost roughly $193, but p2 would have about $196 after the trade.

Standard rent for a single house on the dark blue set is $175 and $200. One house on each property would be devastating. A hotel on either space would cost $1500 or $2000. This trade would give p2 immediate access to that heavy rent income.

Marvin Gardens is worth only about $280 and is useless without a yellow monopoly. p4 already owns three yellows, so they would not need it. Selling Park Place to p2 would let them acquire Boardwalk if they ever go bankrupt, giving p4 both dark blue sets. I will not sell Park Place.

I cannot counter the offer with Boardwalk. I lack the cash to build a dark blue set, and New York Avenue is mortgaged. My focus is completing the orange monopoly. Unmortgaging New York Avenue will cost about $110.

Building three houses on the orange set would cost $900. That plus the $110 unmortgage would total roughly $1010. I only have $551 in cash, so this is impossible. I will reject the trade outright.

I will keep my public message consistent and firm. I briefly considered whether a large cash offer could justify selling Park Place, but rejected it because creating a dark blue monopoly for p2 would be far more dangerous than any benefit. I am now calculating whether I could safely build the orange set to three houses while surviving.

I calculated the total needed to safely build the orange set to three houses. Unmortgaging New York Avenue costs $110, nine houses cost $900, and a buffer for one light blue hotel is about $600. That brings the total to roughly $1610. I can mortgage my pink properties and Water Works for about $215 in cash. I cannot mortgage St James Place while I want to build on it.
